<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
The PKGBUILD defines standard sources: a desktop file and icon fetched via HTTPS from the project's own GitHub repository, and a prebuilt binary for x86_64 also downloaded over HTTPS from the official GitHub releases page. The URLs use command substitution with `${url}`, `${pkgver}`, and `${_pkgname}`, but these are safely derived from declared variables and point to the expected upstream.

Fetching these sources via `makepkg --nobuild --nodeps --noprepare` is safe: the operations involve only downloading and extracting files (or in this case, placing downloaded binaries and assets into the source tree), with no execution of downloaded code. The `sha256sums` and `sha256sums_x86_64` arrays contain valid checksums, so integrity verification will occur during source extraction — though even if they were 'SKIP', that would not make this step unsafe per the gate criteria.

No top-level command substitutions, `pkgver()` function, or other executable code outside of `package()` exists in the PKGBUILD. Therefore, sourcing this PKGBUILD during `makepkg --printsrcinfo` or source fetching does not trigger any dangerous behavior. The commands will only download verifiable, expected assets from the project's official repository.
</details>
<summary>
Safe: No malicious code in sourcing or fetching.
</summary>
</security_assessment>
